artifact: seL4 microkernel Isabelle/HOL proofs (https://github.com/seL4/l4v) for the configurations listed as *_verified.cmake in seL4's configs/ folder; see https://docs.sel4.systems/projects/sel4/verified-configurations.html
property: Functional correctness of the kernel C code against its abstract specification; integrity and confidentiality; on AArch32 (ARM) also binary correctness of the compiled kernel.
model: The preprocessed kernel C source (kernel_all_pp.c) for one fixed verified configuration, over a hardware model in which the MMU fully controls memory; machine interface and boot code are assumptions.
trusted_base: C compiler on configurations without binary-correctness proof (e.g. AARCH64, X64)
assumptions: DMA is off or performed only by trusted devices/drivers
the system is configured per the security-proof conditions
no covert timing channels claimed absent (confidentiality excludes timing)
single-core: multicore verification is in progress
deployed: An seL4 build in a configuration outside the verified set, e.g. with SMMU/IOMMU (VT-d) support, multicore SMP, debug/printing interfaces, or DMA-capable untrusted drivers; or an AArch64 build relying on the compiler.
gap: The proof applies only to the exact verified configurations and assumes DMA off or trusted, correct boot code and assembly; IOMMU/SMMU support, debug interfaces, multicore, and kernel startup are explicitly unverified, and on AArch64 only C-level (not binary) correctness is proved, so any deployment using those features or that compiler path runs outside the proof.

sources.quote: At present, none of our verified configurations take into account address translation for devices (System MMU or IOMMU), debug/profiling/printing interfaces, or the kernel startup at boot.
